newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali opposition stages polls protest.
newsitem.headline: Nepali opposition stages polls protest.

text.p: More than 10,000 supporters of the main opposition Nepali Congress Party held a protest rally on Sunday in Kathmandu, accusing the ruling coalition's dominant communists of rigging last month's local elections, party officials said.
"The protest is to oppose the extensive rigging engineered by the government," Mahesh Acharya a Nepali Congress Party official, told Reuters.
At least six people died in violence during the vote, which elected nearly 190,000 representatives in 4,000 villages and 58 municipalities.
Latest results show that the United Marxist-Leninist party (UML), the dominant partner of the ruling coalition, had won over 91,000 seats.
Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand's Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) had won 22,000 while the protesting Nepali Congress party had 53,000, election commision officials said.
Officials have ordered voting to be repeated in 437 places affected by violence and complete results are expected in another 10 days' time, they said.
Earlier this week Foreign Minister Prakash Chandra Lohani of the RPP quit the government, alleging widespread rigging and intimidation by the UML party in the May 17 and 26 vote.
